title: Invariant discrete quotients and their canonical refinement diagram
statement: Use the small representatives of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be a group acting on a topological space $P$. An invariant discrete quotient is a discrete quotient equivalence relation $s$ on $P$ such that $x\sim_s y$ implies $gx\sim_s gy$ for every $g\in G$. Its quotient topology is discrete, so its classes are nonempty clopen blocks; if $P$ is compact there are finitely many blocks. Order these quotients by inclusion of equivalence relations (a finer partition is smaller). Define the canonical diagram to topological spaces by sending $s$ to its quotient set with its discrete quotient topology and a refinement $s\leq t$ to the map $[x]_s\mapsto[x]_t$. The index is a small type of relations on $P$.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28: finite discrete G-sets and profinite continuous G-sets; invariant version of the quotient partitions in Stacks topology.tex, Tag 08ZY.
